# API fixtures

Payloads captured from the running backend for the seeded synthetic well, so component tests fail
when the frontend drifts from the contract the API actually serves.

Captured with `backend/.venv/bin/python scripts/capture_frontend_fixtures.py` (seeds a throwaway
database under `/tmp`, starts the real API on `127.0.0.1:8093`, records the responses, stops):

| File | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| `well-state.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/state` |
| `well-npt.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/npt` |
| `well-timeline.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/timeline` |
| `well-twin.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/twin` |
| `well-audit.json` | `GET /api/v1/wells/{well_id}/audit` |
| `run-waiting-approval.json` | `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}` while the run waits at `human.approval` |
| `run-succeeded.json` | `GET /api/v1/runs/{run_id}` after the approval was decided and the run resumed |
| `approval-pending.json` | `GET /api/v1/approvals/{approval_id}` before the decision |
| `approvals-list.json` | `GET /api/v1/approvals?status=pending` |
| `approvals-list-any.json` | `GET /api/v1/approvals?status=any` (the decided approval, with its note) |
| `runs-list.json` | `GET /api/v1/runs?limit=50` |

The run and approval fixtures are **trimmed deterministically** by the capture script: the seeded
engineering context is delivered as a ~52 KB generated prompt string that appears in several places in
one payload, and no test reads its text. Strings longer than 2000 characters become
`⟪trimmed: N characters of generated context text⟫`, and flat lists longer than 5 entries keep their
first 5 plus a marker. Every key, type, number and short string is exactly what the server sent.

The well is generated demo data (`SYNTH-DEMO-01 (synthetic data)`), so these files contain no
customer, well or field data. Every identifier inside them (`wel_…`, `opr_…`, `run_…`, `apr_…`) belongs
to that synthetic well and is regenerated by the seeder, which is why the tests read the ids from the
fixtures instead of hard-coding them.

These are contract anchors, not golden files: when the API changes shape on purpose, recapture them
from the real endpoint and commit the change in the same commit as the frontend fix that consumes it.
